title: Fermat from scratch, working alone vs OSO: one traditional run beside the earlier OSO α 0.2 run, 4 labs, $2 a lab, 100 rounds (Nov 24)
question: On one deep problem, Fermat's little theorem built from scratch, do labs get further for the same money when they share every result at once and credit flows back (OSO, α 0.2), or when each keeps its work private until it has proved the theorem (traditional)? One run each: a first look, not a test. [A]
answer: Further with OSO, in this one look. Working alone (traditional), the labs did not prove Fermat in 100 rounds and reached 27 of the 95 hidden steps by $2 a run; the OSO run had reached 52 and went on to prove it. One run a side on different days: the direction is clear, the size is not estimated.

results.heading: Deep set: traditional on Fermat's little theorem (one run, 2026-11-24 to 25)
results.html:
Result. Setup: traditional (public when a target is proved, α 1, m 0, m_bit 0, f 0), otherwise as section 4j: 4 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash labs, $2 a lab, up to 100 rounds, labs cannot stop. One run, on a different day from the OSO run: a first look, not a test (an exception to 5 runs per setup, by choice). With one target, nothing is public until P1 is proved, so each lab works alone.

Result: P1 was not proved in 100 rounds; the run spent $4.65. Labs proved 175 lemmas, 22 of them a second time (another lab had it privately), and no result built on another lab's work. 34 of the 95 hidden steps were reached (Lean, both matcher passes).

Against the OSO run (section 4j), at the same money (scripts/deep-steps.ts, $2 a run): traditional reached 27 hidden steps, deepest level 7; OSO reached 52, deepest level 8, and went on to prove P1 for $2.53. One run a side, different days: the direction is what sharing predicts, the size is not estimated. A shared-library run and fresh runs of both are going (deep-fermat-2).

Harness: 47% of this run's replies were cut off before an answer. (The OSO run predates logging of the stop reason, so its 43% in section 4j was counted from empty replies.)
